finding.title: Refresh learning_tracker/dart_test.yaml's stale tag registry

evidence.quote: # Prevents "unknown tag" warnings when running flutter test --tags.

finding.why: Comparing every tag declared in dart_test.yaml against every tag actually used via `@Tags([...])`/`tags: [...]` across learning_tracker/test/ (`comm -23` on the two sorted sets) shows 295 of 400 used tags are undeclared — including entire epics that clearly exist and have Makefile targets (epic_18, epic_20, epic_24, epic_28) plus dozens of story tags (story_15_2/4/7/9/11/13/15/16/17, story_18_*, story_25_2/9/22, story_26_23/31, story_27_5/14, story_i3/i4, and ~200 ad-hoc descriptive tags like `widget`, `unit`, `a11y`, `rtl`). The file's stated one job — suppressing 'unknown tag' warnings — now fails for most of the suite, defeating its purpose and adding warning noise that makes genuine problems easy to miss in CI logs.
finding.recommendation: Regenerate the tags: block from a script that scans test/ for all @Tags()/tags: usages, or drop the file if package:test's current version no longer warns on undeclared tags.
acceptance_criteria: `comm -23` between tags used in test/ and tags declared in dart_test.yaml is empty.

finding.title: Fix inconsistent check-count labels in learning_tracker/Makefile's audit target

evidence.quote: echo "16/17 — No raw profile.mode string comparisons (use ProfileMode enum) (W5.10)"; \
echo "18/18 — No direct FirestoreGateway.push* outside lib/core/sync/ (Plan §F Phase 5 deliverable 8 — no-direct-gateway-push)"; \
echo "20/22 — No raw curriculumId/storageKey rendered in Text() (render via CurriculumLabel / rendered*ForRef)"; \

finding.why: The 22 checks are echoed as 1/15...15/15, then 16/17, 17/17, 18/18, 19/20, 20/22, 21/22, 22/22 — five different denominators (15, 17, 18, 20, 22) across one run, none matching the actual total until the very last line. This is harmless to the pass/fail logic but actively misleading to anyone reading `make audit` output while debugging a failure (e.g. 'check 18/18' reads as the last check, when 4 more follow) — clear evidence checks were bolted on over time without updating earlier labels.
finding.recommendation: Renumber every echo label to X/22 in one pass.
acceptance_criteria: Every numbered echo in the audit target uses a consistent /22 denominator.

finding.title: Remove or repair the dead root firebase.json/.firebaserc pointing at missing files
finding.why: Root firebase.json references firestore.rules and firestore.indexes.json relative to the repo root, but neither file exists there — both live only under learning_tracker/. `firebase deploy`/`firebase emulators:start` run from the repo root (a natural instinct since .firebaserc's project default lives there too) would fail immediately with a file-not-found error. Git history confirms firestore.rules used to live at repo root and was moved under learning_tracker/ during a restructure, with the root firebase.json/.firebaserc never cleaned up. Compounding this, no Makefile or CI workflow in the repo contains a `firebase deploy` or `firebase use` command anywhere — there is no committed, automated path from the source-controlled firestore.rules to the real deployed ruleset at all.
finding.recommendation: Delete the root firebase.json/.firebaserc (or repoint them at learning_tracker/), and document (or automate via CI on tag/release) the actual firestore.rules deploy process.
acceptance_criteria: Root firebase.json's referenced paths exist, or the file is removed.

finding.title: Remove the inert .gitattributes merge=beads directive for a gitignored path
finding.why: `.beads/` is git-ignored at the repo root, and `git ls-files | grep beads` confirms `.beads/issues.jsonl` has never been tracked. A `merge=` custom-merge-driver attribute only ever activates during a git merge of a tracked file, so this line can never fire. Even setting that aside, no `merge.beads.driver` command is registered anywhere in the repo (no hooks/, tool/, or doc sets it via `git config`) — so even a force-added copy of the file would hit 'unable to find custom merge driver beads' rather than actually merging. This is dead scaffolding for a workflow (the beads issue tracker) that isn't wired into this repo.
finding.recommendation: Either delete the .gitattributes line (if beads isn't used here), or un-ignore .beads/issues.jsonl and add a committed setup step that registers `git config merge.beads.driver`.
acceptance_criteria: Either .gitattributes no longer references a driver that's never registered, or the driver is registered by a committed script and the target path is tracked.

finding.title: Extract duplicated CI bootstrap steps into a shared composite action

evidence.quote:
# Shared Flutter + pub setup extracted via composite action pattern (inline reuse via YAML anchors)
# GitHub Actions does not support YAML anchors natively, so setup steps are duplicated per job.

finding.why: ci.yml's own comment justifies duplicating checkout/Flutter-setup/pub-cache/codegen/secret-decode steps ACROSS ITS OWN JOBS because 'GitHub Actions does not support YAML anchors natively' — true, but the actual GHA-native fix (composite actions / reusable workflows via `uses:`) is never used, and the same six-to-eight-step bootstrap sequence is copy-pasted a further two times whole across build.yml and deploy-play-store.yml (which the stated per-job-isolation rationale doesn't even apply to — they're separate files, not parallel jobs needing independent runners). A future change to how secrets are decoded or how the seed asset is prepared requires finding and editing this sequence in up to 6 places (4 ci.yml jobs + build.yml + deploy-play-store.yml) with no mechanism to catch a missed one.
finding.recommendation: Create `.github/actions/flutter-bootstrap/action.yml` (checkout+setup+cache+codegen+asset-prep+secret-decode) and reference it via `uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-bootstrap` from all three workflow files.
acceptance_criteria: A single composite action exists and build.yml, ci.yml, and deploy-play-store.yml all invoke it instead of repeating the step sequence inline.
